transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, things have just been a little stressful lately, you know? I work as a diesel mechanic, so the shifts are pretty long and tiring. 

I don't think it's a huge deal, but I've noticed that sometimes when I get home from work, I just... I end up eating a bit more than I probably should. Like, I might grab a fast-food meal on the way home, and then maybe have some snacks, and then kind of just graze on whatever else is in the fridge. All at once, I mean. It's just a way to unwind, I think. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this right.
When you find yourself eating more than you probably should after work, do you feel like you can stop eating if you wanted to, or does it feel more like you can't control it once you start?

Well, I mean, usually I've got pretty good self-control. I don't want you to think I'm just completely off the rails or anything. But... yeah, I guess on those specific nights, it's, um... it is really hard to stop. 

To be honest, once I start on those nights, it almost feels like my hands just keep grabbing for more food on their own. Even while I’m sitting there telling myself to just quit it, and I’m already feeling sick to my stomach, I just keep going. It's pretty embarrassing to admit that. I hope that doesn't sound too crazy... is that something you hear from other people? I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right.
After these eating episodes, do you find yourself feeling guilty, ashamed, or really hard on yourself about what you ate?

Um, well, I guess nobody really feels great after eating too much, right? I mean, it's not like I'm sitting there crying about it or anything dramatic. I'm a pretty positive guy overall. 

But, yeah, I do feel a little... I don't know, maybe a bit disappointed in myself? Just because I know I shouldn't be eating all that junk, especially when I need to stay sharp for work the next day. It's more of a "man, why did I do that again" kind of feeling than, like, deep shame or anything. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea—does that sound like a normal reaction to you?

After these episodes where you feel like you've eaten more than you intended, do you ever try to make up for it by doing something like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

Um... well... I mean, I definitely don't want you to think I have some kind of huge problem, because I really try to keep things under control. But... yeah, I guess I do sometimes try to, you know, fix it after I eat like that. 

It's just... I get kind of freaked out about what all that food is going to do to me, especially since I need to stay in decent shape for the shop. So, um, sometimes I might... well, I might go to the bathroom and sort of make myself throw up. Or occasionally I'll take some laxatives, just to kind of clear things out and get a fresh start. It's not an everyday thing, I promise! Just when I feel really stuffed and worried. Is... is that something that happens with other people? I just want to make sure I'm not sounding totally out there.
How often do you find yourself making yourself vomit or taking laxatives after these eating episodes—like, would you say it happens once a week, a few times a month, or less often than that?

Um... well, it's really not like an everyday thing, I want to be clear about that. I definitely don't let it interfere with my job at the shop or anything. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it's probably, um, most weeks. 

Like, most weeks there's at least one night where I kind of overdo it on the eating and then... you know, try to fix it. Whether that's throwing up, or taking the laxatives, or sometimes just skipping meals the next day or pushing myself really hard at the gym. And, um, I guess it's been happening like that for a few months now. Several months, maybe. 

I really try to keep it under control, though. I hope that doesn't sound too bad? Like, once a week isn't the worst thing in the world, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
